market: The Strait of Hormuz standoff drove PSX lower for a fourth straight session: Brent crude pushed toward $90/bbl (last ~$89.53) and WTI near $84 as attacks on regional shipping dented hopes of a near-term US-Iran deal to reopen the strait — the US EIA now doesn't expect Middle East oil production back near pre-conflict levels until early 2027. KSE-100 opened firm (intraday high 181,017) but selling intensified through the session to close down 1,464 points (-0.81%) at 179,846.68, broad-based again across autos, cement, banks, fertiliser, E&P and OMCs (Fauji Fertiliser, Engro Holdings, Lucky Cement, UBL, BAHL, OGDC and Hub Power were the biggest index drags). Against the Jan 23, 2026 all-time high of 189,556, the drawdown has widened to roughly 5.12% (from ~5.0% yesterday) — the fourth consecutive daily widening, still comfortably clear of the 10% line that would trigger deploying the AICF/MICF cash reserve, but the trend is now four sessions old and worth watching closely if Hormuz drags on. SBP's policy rate remains at 11.5% (held Jul 27, second consecutive pause); no new IMF program developments. Mali's price feed (stamped 2026-08-12T08:24:39Z, ~1hr before close) shows no holding moving even 2% day-over-day since yesterday — DCR +1.14% and FABL +0.83% were the day's best, MEBL -0.66% and UPFL -0.71% the softest; genuinely quiet at the position level even as the index fell. DATA QUALITY — root cause found and fixed this review: fund NAVs (ASSF, AKDISSF, NISIF, NISF, MIF, AICF, MICF) had been frozen at their Aug 4 values for 8 straight days despite the Aug 4 commit (d4e0d2d) fixing the original 403/WAF block. Checked scripts/fetch_prices.py and the GitHub Actions run history directly: the daily runs since (e.g. Aug 11 17:25 UTC) all reported "success" at the job level while matching zero NAV rows — but the local working tree already contained a further, un-pushed fix (throttle the MUFAP scrape to once/day at 16:30 UTC instead of hitting it ~40x/day alongside the stock-price cron, since over-scraping had likely gotten the Actions IP range re-blocked; plus a retry-once pass and explicit staleness logging) that a prior session had written but never committed. That fix was sitting locally, unpushed, so GitHub Actions kept executing the old broken code on every scheduled run. Committed and pushed it this review (workflow now also passes CRON_SCHEDULE so the code can tell which cron fired it) — funds should pick up a live NAV at tonight's 21:30 PKT run; if they're still frozen tomorrow, the block itself needs a deeper look rather than the throttle theory. Fund P/L below is stale by up to 8 days as of this review. On holdings: EFERT — no news since the confirmed Aug 5 briefing (no planned price discounts, management expects H2 farmer demand to clear the ~694K ton urea inventory glut); ex-dividend already passed Aug 10, still on WATCH into Q3 results. AVN — no fresh company news again; position unchanged at the full 24,500 shares, Rs 32.40 today (-0.6% day-over-day, -28.1% on cost), the stated "Monday Aug 3's open" execution window is now 9 days gone with no sign the trade happened. Either it was executed off-app and index.html needs updating, or it's still sitting unexecuted — Sep 2, 2026 earnings (3 weeks away) remains the hard exit deadline. CPHL — no update since the Jul 8 REIT-demerger approval, roughly flat today (-0.16%). No holdings-file edits today — qty/avg figures unchanged.
